name: Kosha Mangsho
ingredients: 1 kg mutton (goat meat) on the bone
Whole spices (2 bay leaves, 4 green cardamoms, 4 cloves, 1-inch cinnamon stick)
instructions: 1. Marinate the mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, and a tablespoon of mustard oil for at least 2 hours.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and fry the potatoes until golden; remove and set aside.
3. In the same oil, add sugar and let it caramelize until deep brown, then add whole spices.
4. Sauté the sliced onions until soft and translucent.
5. Add the marinated mutton and cook on high heat, stirring continuously, to 'koshano' (sauté) the meat until it releases its juices and oil begins to separate.
6. Add the powdered spices (cumin, coriander, chili) and cook for another 10 minutes.
7. Pour in warm water, add the fried potatoes, cover, and cook on low heat until the meat is tender and the gravy is thick and dark.
8. Rest for 10 minutes before serving with luchi or basmati rice.
description: Kosha Mangsho is an iconic Bengali delicacy, traditionally prepared during Sunday lunches or festivals like Durga Puja. The term 'Kosha' refers to the slow-frying technique of the spice base, resulting in a dark, succulent, and flavor-packed mutton dish that embodies the culinary heritage of Bengal.
